title: Mid-Michigan businesses get nearly $850K in job training grants - NewsBreak
text:
By Shajaka Shelton No media credit provided. ,
2 hours ago
LANSING, Mich. (WLNS) — Mid-Michigan businesses received nearly $850,000 in grant funding from the state to support the training of their workers, the Michigan Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity announced Tuesday.
“Michigan’s economic success depends on connecting people to opportunity and helping businesses build the skilled workforce they need,” LEO Workforce Development Director Krista Johnson said. “Together, these investments are strengthening communities and supporting long-term growth across our state.”
These grants were just some of more than $6 million handed out in this year’s second cycle of the Going PRO Talent Fund program, which the department says help Michigan workers train and advance in high-demand, high-skill careers.
Lansing economic report shows strong investment in Mid-Michigan “These grants help workers gain valuable skills and credentials while providing employers with the talent they need to grow, compete and succeed in Michigan’s economy,” LEO Director Susan Corbin said.
The fund supports several different types of “employer-led” training options, including classroom instruction, on-the-job training and apprenticeships. According to LEO, workers who complete Talent-Fund-supported training see an average hourly wage increase of 6.2%.
A list of Mid-Michigan grant recipients can be found below. To view the full list of statewide recipients or to learn more about the grant program, you can do so on the state’s website .
